rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: adding buffer and dependency checks [Action]
rows.description: The developer maps that testing needs the client's sandbox, which takes a week to arrive. She requests it today and adds a two-day buffer before the promised date.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, minimum viable version, planning fallacy, prioritising, task decomposition

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: asking the manager what is driving the date [Thinking]
rows.description: Rather than arguing about days, she asks why the date matters. It is a board meeting on the 20th, so a working demo is enough and a full release can follow later.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, buffer and slack, commitment device, minimum viable version, planning fallacy, prioritising

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: early risk flag with updated forecast [Revision]
rows.description: Midway, a vendor delay appears. She tells the manager the same day, shares a revised date, and suggests one task be moved to another team, avoiding a last-minute surprise.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, commitment device, minimum viable version, planning fallacy, prioritising, task decomposition

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: written follow-up to record the agreement [Action]
rows.description: After the discussion she emails the manager a short summary of what was agreed, what is deferred and why. This avoids later disputes about what was promised.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, commitment device, minimum viable version, planning fallacy, prioritising, task decomposition

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: preparing facts, cause and options first [Thinking]
rows.description: Before telling a hospital client that go-live will slip by three weeks, the account lead gathers the cause, the new date and two ways to reduce impact, so the message has substance.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation, mental simulation

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of likely reactions [Thinking]
rows.description: He imagines the client being angry, asking whom to blame, or asking for a discount. He drafts calm, honest replies for each so he is not pushed into rash promises.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: calling directly before sending an email [Action]
rows.description: Instead of a written notice, he phones the client the same morning, states the delay in the first minute, then sends a summary email so both have a record.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation, mental simulation

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: delaying until a fix is found [Pitfall]
rows.description: Hoping to solve it quietly, the manager waits two weeks before telling the client. When the delay is finally revealed, trust suffers more than the delay itself would have caused.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation, mental simulation

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: softening so much that the message is unclear [Pitfall]
rows.description: The messenger says things are progressing but may take a little longer. The client hears a small tweak and plans around the old date, then reacts badly when it moves a month.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation, mental simulation

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: consulting the senior leader on framing [Thinking]
rows.description: Unsure how much to disclose, the team lead asks her director about the tone and about whether to offer a service credit. The director joins the call to show seriousness.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, delegation, mental simulation
